newsitem.title: LATVIA: BOURSE CHIEF SEES $1.0 BLN MKT CAP BY END 1997.
newsitem.headline: BOURSE CHIEF SEES $1.0 BLN MKT CAP BY END 1997.

text.p: Latvian bourse chief Uldis Cerps on Monday said that he expected a wave of privatisations this year to take the market capitalisation of the stock exchange to one billion dollars.
He pointed out that the privatisations of Latvenergo, Ventspils Nafta and Latvian Gas would all help to increase the market capitalisation to around 20 percent of GDP.

"What we are seeing is that as these privatisations are completed, the market capitalisation should grow to one billion dollars," he told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) in an interview in London.
Market capitalisation is currently around $330 million or eight percent of GDP.
Cerps also said that an agreement with Estonia on linking their central depositories would be good for foreign and local investors alike.
"It will be a user-friendly environment for custody. This means that foreign investors do not need three custody arrangements," he added.
But he said that a true pan-Baltic market would need time to be formed.
"The most important thing is to have strong domestic markets," he said. "Once you have got three strong local markets then you can have one market."
